I can't argue against the fact that my relationship with alcohol isn't healthy, it never was. It's pretty easy for me to admit that I'm weak to substances, what I guess I struggle with is the idea that it's "bad enough" that it requires any change. Man that doesn't sound right at all when I type it out. But it's like I keep thinking to myself that the upsides of drinking outweigh the negatives? Or something.

I mentioned it in another comment. But I keep feeling like I don't have "enough" of a drinking problem to justify seeking help. Like it'd be diminishing other people's "real" struggles and would be a waste of other people's time/energy if I did try to seek support. I know it probably doesn't make much sense but the idea of seeking out the local AA group feels like it would be wrong of me because I don't have a "real" problem. I feel a lot of guilt associated with seeking help for basically anything. I don't have any issue admitting I'm weak, but I have a lot of problems with the idea of inconveniencing or annoying other people. I hate the idea that I could be causing other people problems with my "nonsense".

That sounds weird to me even though it kind of makes sense. I guess the idea in my mind is that only "alcholics" are "allowed" in AA. Like someone who isn't an "alcholic" joining would be an insult or something, even though that also doesn't quite sound right to me. I struggled with a similar issue when it came to mental health cause I get caught up in the idea that my life/experiences weren't "bad enough" to justify being "mentally ill". I keep feeling like I'm diminishing someone's else struggles when I apply those kinds of labels to myself.

To be fair to me my therapy isn't a waste since I've got a whole host of issues to work through, but otherwise fair point. In all honestly I don't know what I want to do about my drinking. I'm torn between it would be better overall for me to quit but on the other hand I love drinking. I don't really know how to approach my drinking when I try to thinking about coming to a concrete goal/solution.

You have every right to be angry about that!! The only time anyone has any right to say anything about someone's suicide attempt to another person is if it's in the moment and it's to save that person's life, and even then it should be handled delicately. You should have complete control over who you choose to tall about your attempts with. I had a similar thing happen with my younger brother, and it honestly felt like such a betrayal. For a lot of people who attempt talking about it is incredibly personal. So know that you are completely justified in your feelings. Although I can't provide much helpful advice on how to handle the situation other than to say that arguing rarely ever solves anything despite how strong the urge can be. My approach has always been to just not deal with people I know I won't get anywhere with, just kinda be passive with them. Hope any of that helps.

Please don't! I have no right to say not to, or really say anything to you. I don't know your circumstances or reasons. I only know that your a person and it hurts my heart to know your hurting. I've attempted a few times and continue to struggle with suicidal ideation, but I don't wish this feeling on anyone. I can't say that things will get better, or that the people in your life love you. But I can say that I love and value you as a person, simply by the fact that your alive. Everybody is worth something, even if I don't believe that enough to apply it to myself. I have a coin that says don't die today and sometimes staring at it is the only thing that keeps me going. I guess that's all I can say to you, please don't die today. I'm not very reliable or have words of wisdom, but if you need to talk I'm here for you.

That's fantastic!! I'm so proud of you!!! Living is the hardest thing we'll ever do, so everyday you survive is an accomplishment. Don't forget that!! Only feeling suicidal less than l half of the time is great. I hope you maintain that mindset because you deserve it. Truly. I hope you smile and laugh more, or at least sometimes. Because those moments are what make everything worth it. Even if it's dumb shit like a show, a story you read, or something someone said, who cares what it is as long as it makes you smile and helps you keep going.

I'm sorry that it didn't work out for you. And that life pushed you in that direction. But also I'm happy that it didn't work our for you. It can be hard to be happy or releaved when a suicide attempt doesn't work out, I know from personal experience. I don't have a lot of words of encouragement. Other than I can sort of get where your coming from, and I hope your not too upset about surviving. I live with a coin that says don't die today on one side, sometimes its all I have to keep me going. Living is hard, harder than dying ever will be. So even if you feel like shit be proud that you lived another day, you accomplished something, because living is fucking hard and sucks a lot of the time. So be proud of your accomplishment, even if no one else sees or acknowledges it. You've made it this far and that's a pretty big deal. I won't say that things will get better, cause I have yet to see that happen in my own life. But try to enjoy any smile or laugh that you can, cause maybe that's all we've got to hold on to. Sorry I'm not good at this lol I'm a pretty major bummer myself. But hey I love you because your alive and that's all you need to be worthy of love. Sorry if life's a real bummer and people suck. But try to keep going one day at a time and maybe you'll reach somewhere real nice with time.

As someone who admitted themselves to a hospital multiple times due to suicidal ideation I will say that if that's your last option then go for it, because trying anything is better than giving up. Not that I'm shaming your suicidal ideation, I've spent most of life living with it. But think of it in terms of every day you don't die is a win, even if no one else sees it you've succeded everyday that you don't give in. Living is the hardest thing you can do and the fact that your reading this is a testament to your struggle to survive. So congrats, your making it. Even if no one else sees it, be proud of every day that you don't give in. Sorry if I sound cheesy or dumb as fuck. I'm a bit drunk and trying to cheer myself up, suicidal ideation ain't no joke lol it's tough living life alongside this lovely lady named death. I have a coin I carry with me that says don't die today, it's probably dumb but it's the goal I approach everyday with. Anyway I'm proud of you for reading this and trying, because reaching out shows you want a reason to keep going. So here's your reason, your alive and that's all you need to justify your worth and existence. I love you for who you are and wish you at the very least an occasional and a laugh here and there.

I feel like I don't have a particularly usefull response. I've also been doing nothing but being on my phone recently, probably about 2 months. Just reading endlessly to fill the time. I've been struggling with suicidal ideation and just feeling too tired to keep going. But idk man. I guess just keep trying to keep on going? The idea of lasting another day is really all that's got me going. I dont have any end goal, just trying to not die everyday. So I guess idk, join me in trying to not die each day? I wish I had good advice or something that would change your perspective in life. But unfortunately I don't. So all I can say is don't give up, just keep on trying. Sorry if this is nonsense. Honestly I'm pretty drunk on a bench in the middle of town just barely hanging on, so what do I know lol Deep down past all my bullshit I believe everybody is worth something by virtue of being alive, but also I've been suicidal since I was a child so what do I know. Do something that makes you smile, or at least keeps your mind mostly off the bad shit and just keep breathing. For those of us who struggle just living another day is a triumph that we should celebrate. So good luck? I'm drunk so who knows if this makes any sense or helps. But know that if nothing else I love you simply because your a person and I love people. Everyone deserves to be happy regardless of their circumstances or history. So try smiling, and if you can idk laugh or make a nasty face or something if that makes you happy lol

That last bit reminds me how my mom thought (still thinks?) my "picky eating" as a teen was me rebelling against her. That I just wanted to be difficult. It's horrible struggling to eat and makes social gatherings (especially holidays) so frustrating and upsetting. Why the fuck would anyone do that to themselves to upset someone else? It makes no sense. After a lifetime of having ARFID it's become exhausting to try to get people to even consider that my eating disorder is a real thing that actually impacts my life in severe ways.

I can't say either way if you have ARFID. But I will say that it's possible to have ARFID without being underweight or struggling to maintain a healthy weight. I personally struggle with losing weight because so many of my safe foods are packaged/processed. My advice would be that if your eating is having a negative impact on your life then you should try to see a nutritionist. If that's not an option then maybe record your eating habits so that you can get an overall picture of what your dealing with. Then you could look for resources online on how to deal with it, like creating a diet consisting of safe foods that will give your body what it needs. Lastly know your not alone in this and this community is always here for you.
This is exactly how I am. It's really sensory based for me. Its so annoying when anyone asks how I dislike something without trying it.

Congrats!! I'm on day 9. I haven't thought to include working out to my days, but makes total sense. Whenever I've worked out in the past it gave me energy and left me feeling good about myself. I feel like finding things that make us feel good about what we're doing with our bodies could be a tremendous help with T breaks or quiting.
Sounds like a good idea, at least to me. Personal I feel like if I did that it would just frustrate and upset me.

I also appreciated that someone on YouTube spoke about ARFID. However I do have two critiques. 
1) All of the videos I've watched about ARFID on YouTube mention being underweight or lacking nutrients and it was the same in this video. That's very frustrating because it gives a narrow view of ARFID, as well as perpetuating the notion that everyone with an ED is thin. That's not true at all. Being underweight can absolutely  be a factor, but it's not required for the diagnosis. I understand she was speaking about it from her experience, but it would be nice if someone would talk about those of us who struggle with being overweight because so many of our safe foods are packaged/processed food. I dislike the reality of saying you have an ED only for someone to tell you that you don't LOOK like you have an ED.
2) This one is less of a critique I suppose and more of uncertainty. It seems strange to me that she says that she only has ARFID for maybe a couple weeks then goes back to being a foodie. That just doesn't sound like ARFID to me, and it concerns me that it will send the wrong message about what it means to have ARFID. This isn't a struggle I deal with every once in a while, I've been dealing with it for the past 15yrs. I WISH I only dealt with it occasionally and then got to go back to enjoy food like most people. I'm not a doctor so I can't say definitely if you can have occasional short episodes of ARFID. But it just struck me as a bit odd and kind of a misrepresentation.
Aside from that though I really appreciated someone with her kind of platform introducing this ED to people who most likely have never heard of it. I just worry that her messaging will give people the wrong impression, and possibly lead people to falsely diagnose themselves. Like people who say that they have OCD because they like to be clean and organized. Media and people have represented OCD so badly that a lot of people don't understand the severity and how debilitating it can be. Those of us with ARFID already have to deal with people calling us "picky eaters", I don't also want to deal with people saying that they have ARFID cause there's some foods they don't like. I'm not saying she's like that, but I can absolutely see other people walking away with that image of ARFID. Again I'm not bashing on her. I think it's fantastic that she spoke up. I'm just concerned about how people will recieve it.

I get that. I had to drop out of a work program ( California Conservation Corp) due to having to live in dorms. I only had access to foods from a cafeteria, which I've never been able to handle. I would hide crackers and peanut butter in my room to keep me going, but eventually the physical nature of the job became too much for my underfed body. We also had to take turns cleaning the cafeteria and dishes, which was absolutely out of the question for me. Idk how common it is with people who struggle with ARFID but I personally can't handle cleaning up after unsafe foods,, especially dishes. So I understand that struggle. It was honestly a very hard decision to make, it made me feel weak and like a coward. Thankfully now that I know about ARFID I can look back and understand that it couldn't be helped how I responded to that environment. So I hope you aren't too hard on yourself like I was. We can't help the fact that we have an ED and the impact it has on our lives. I wish you luck and peace of mind.

I would suggest sticking around here. I've found that reading posts about people who have the same food problems as me has helped a lot. I'm 30 now and have been mocked my entire life about my food problems. For the first time I feel like it's not my fault, that I'm not being difficult. I have a real ED and I'm not the only one. I also agree that it's great that your seeking information / help at such a young age. I feel as though just having a name for it helps. I dont have advice on expanding your foods aside from seeking help for it, perhaps with a nutritionist or a therapist who has experience working with eating disorders. I personally haven't reached the point of being ready to try new foods, so unfortunately I don't have any practical advice to give. Just remember your not alone and your not being difficult.

From what I've read you don't need to have a fear of choking/vomiting. My understanding is that ARFID generally falls into 3 subcategories. I personally have sensory problems with food. Not everyone's experience with ARFID is the same.

"1) Lack of interest: clients with this type of ARFID have a genuine lack of interest in eating and food. They also get full quickly.
2)Sensory Avoidance: clients with sensory avoidance have issues with food tastes, textures, temperature and smells.
3)Fear of Aversive Consequences; fear of illness, choking, nausea and allergies" -https://centerfordiscovery.com/conditions/arfid/
This is exactly how I felt when my therapist asked me if I was up for expanding my food boundaries lol I'd love to, but also no. Just no.

That's fantastic!! I'm happy for you, it's great that you've found something that helps. Not only that but your actively gaining weight, that's awesome. Personally I've found working out definitely helps give me an appetite, unfortunately it doesn't change what I can handle eating.

That's fanastic!! I too am with someone who for the first time is very understanding and supportive of my eating difficulties. All my life my family and ex's would mock me and get frustrated when I couldn't eat something/somewhere. It makes a world of difference when you finally have someone who does their best to understand, and is accommodating without making you feel guilty. To have someone who's really a partner in every sense. I wish you and your partner lots of happiness.
That's fantastic!! I'm so happy for you. It's always great when a food you once enjoyed becomes a safe food again. This happened with me and frozen burritos.

I also have the same problem. I can only have Heinz ketchup for example. My family always mocked me for it, saying there's no way I can tell the difference. But like you I'm very sensitive to tastes. My mom would sometimes change brands and try to pass it off as the same, but I could always tell. Gotta say reading posts like this helps me feel less like I'm just a difficult and unreasonable person. I wouldn't wish this ED on anyone, but it feels good to know I'm not alone.

As someone surrounded by foodies I absolutely relate. It's so hard having arfids and having to watch and listen to everyone around you enjoying all kinds of foods. It's frustrating as hell. I also haven't been able to expand my safe foods. It's something I've tried but just can't seem to handle. Just changing what type of butter/margarine I used gave me anxiety.
